1.explanation: The root of the problem is in panel-tabset.lua: the render_tabset function builds the <ul> for the Bootstrap tabs by calling renderer.ulAttribs, which in the bootstrapTabs() definition hard-codes only 'class="nav nav-tabs" role="tablist"'. Any extra class on the original div (like nav-fill) is never propagated into the generated <ul>. The bootstrapTabs.ulAttribs function therefore needs to be updated to merge or pass through the nav-fill class (and any others) from the div attributes when constructing the nav element.
1.bug_scenario: In Quarto 1.3.x the combination of the panel-tabset and nav-fill CSS classes no longer produces a Bootstrap-styled tab bar that stretches to fill the available width. In the prerelease you see a basic stacked panel output instead of a full-width, evenly-spaced nav tab bar. Reversing the class order (putting .nav-fill on the outer container) works around the issue, indicating that the filter is dropping the nav-fill class when both are on the same div.

2.explanation: All of the tab-rendering logic lives in panel-tabset.lua. The AST handler for class_name "panel-tabset" invokes render_tabset with the div’s Attr. In render_tabset, the <ul> is hard-coded to use renderer.ulAttribs(tabsetid), and bootstrapTabs.ulAttribs returns only "class=\"nav nav-tabs\" role=\"tablist\"", ignoring any additional classes (like nav-fill) that were placed on the original div. As a result, nav-fill never gets propagated to the actual <ul> element. To restore the intended behavior, render_tabset (or bootstrapTabs.ulAttribs) must be modified so that it merges any extra classes (including nav-fill) from attr.classes into the <ul> attributes.
2.bug_scenario: The user is combining a panel-tabset with the Bootstrap utility class nav-fill (i.e. using :::{.panel-tabset .nav-fill}). In Quarto 1.2.x the nav-fill class was honored on the generated <ul> so each tab stretched to fill the horizontal space. In 1.3.x the nav-fill class is never applied to the <ul> (only the default nav-tabs classes are used), so the tabs collapse to their content width and do not fill the container. Reversing the class order (nav-fill then panel-tabset) works as a workaround because nav-fill ends up on the outer container, but the intended behavior of applying nav-fill to the tab navigation is broken.
